summary: All 5 phases of the destructive-git guard implemented and verified. git-snapshot.sh (helper) writes a durable working-progress-{ts}.patch under the task dir plus a git stash -u / WIP-branch backup, then refreshes a gitignored .git-snapshot-marker freshness marker (120s window, single-shot/delete-on-use). guard-destructive-git.sh (PreToolUse Bash hook, modeled on block-pr-submission.sh) reads tool_input.command from stdin JSON, exits 0 immediately on a clean tree (auto-exempting /todo's safety-commit + reset --hard/clean -fd flow) or empty command, matches anchored destructive patterns (git reset --hard; git checkout -- <path>; git restore <path> without --staged; git clean with both -f and -d in any order; git stash drop/clear; forced checkout/switch), and blocks via exit 2 + stderr unless a fresh marker is consumed. git-workflow.md gained a 'No Destructive Git on Uncommitted Work' section replacing the old blanket prohibition. All three artifacts were dual-deployed to .claude/extensions/core/ (byte-identical, diff-verified) and wired into manifest.json provides.hooks/provides.scripts plus both settings.json copies (deployed + extension-source root-files). .gitignore gained **/.git-snapshot-marker. IMPORTANT DEVIATION: the settings.json Bash matcher was registered as plain 'bash .claude/hooks/guard-destructive-git.sh' rather than the plan's literal '... 2>/dev/null || echo {}' suffix, because that suffix silently discards the hook's exit-2 block signal and stderr message via bash || semantics, which would have made the entire mechanism a permanent no-op -- this is documented in the plan's Phase 4 checklist and the implementation summary. The hook's live enforcement was confirmed mid-implementation: this session's own Bash tool call was blocked when a test script literally contained 'git clean -qfd', since this repo's real tree is genuinely dirty with other agents' uncommitted work. No destructive git command was run against this repository's actual working tree at any point; all destructive-command testing used disposable /tmp git repos or crafted JSON piped directly to the hook script.
